scenes.tts: The first film used one genome to supply what another lacked. Can a supplied compound reveal where a pathway is blocked? Watch one cell build a needed product through a chain of steps.
scenes.caption: The first film used one genome to supply what another lacked. Can a supplied compound reveal where a pathway is blocked? Watch one cell build a needed product through a chain of steps.
scenes.visual: Hook first, no title card. Reuse the first film's COLOR MAP exactly: blue and gold for distinct functions or steps; green for observed rescue and growth; red for a tested block or failure; gray for inactive context. A large schematic cell contains a left-to-right chain of four labelled blocks: precursor, early intermediate, late intermediate, product. Material moves continuously along arrows. Mark the chain 'schematic'.
scenes.narration: The first film used one genome to supply what another lacked. Can a supplied compound reveal where a pathway is blocked? Watch one cell build a needed product through a chain of steps.

scenes.tts: Each arrow needs a gene-controlled function. A damaging mutation can remove one function and stop the flow. The cell then lacks the final product, even though every step after the block may still work.
scenes.caption: Each arrow needs a gene-controlled function. A damaging mutation can remove one function and stop the flow. The cell then lacks the final product, even though every step after the block may still work.
scenes.visual: Place alternating blue and gold function badges over the arrows. A red barrier drops across the middle arrow. Moving material piles up just before it, but label that pile 'may accumulate'. Downstream arrows continue a faint ready pulse; the product and growth gauge turn gray.
scenes.narration: Each arrow needs a gene-controlled function. A damaging mutation can remove one function and stop the flow. The cell then lacks the final product, even though every step after the block may still work.

scenes.tts: A nutritional screen makes that hidden block visible. Keep each mutant alive on complete medium, then test minimal medium. Adding candidate compounds separately asks which supplied material can restore the missing synthesis and growth.
scenes.caption: A nutritional screen makes that hidden block visible. Keep each mutant alive on complete medium, then test minimal medium. Adding candidate compounds separately asks which supplied material can restore the missing synthesis and growth.
scenes.visual: Transform the cell into a large row of schematic culture dishes. Complete medium stays green for the mutant. Minimal medium turns gray. Candidate supply blocks enter separate minimal dishes one at a time; keep their outcomes unresolved until the pathway returns. Do not show any molecular structures.
scenes.narration: A nutritional screen makes that hidden block visible. Keep each mutant alive on complete medium, then test minimal medium. Adding candidate compounds separately asks which supplied material can restore the missing synthesis and growth.

scenes.tts: Add an upstream intermediate. It enters before the broken arrow and reaches the same barrier. Nothing arrives downstream. The growth gauge stays dark. Failure to rescue tells us only that this supply did not bypass the block.
scenes.caption: Add an upstream intermediate. It enters before the broken arrow and reaches the same barrier. Nothing arrives downstream. The growth gauge stays dark. Failure to rescue tells us only that this supply did not bypass the block.
scenes.visual: A large blue supply block enters the pathway on the left side of the red barrier. It travels right, stops, and joins the schematic pile. Reset the gauge to neutral before revealing a red 'no growth'. Keep downstream steps visible but inactive.
scenes.narration: Add an upstream intermediate. It enters before the broken arrow and reaches the same barrier. Nothing arrives downstream. The growth gauge stays dark. Failure to rescue tells us only that this supply did not bypass the block.

scenes.tts: Now add a downstream intermediate. It enters beyond the broken arrow. The later functions convert it into the needed product, and growth returns. Rescue places the block somewhere before that entry point.
scenes.caption: Now add a downstream intermediate. It enters beyond the broken arrow. The later functions convert it into the needed product, and growth returns. Rescue places the block somewhere before that entry point.
scenes.visual: Clear the red answer before the new case. A gold supply block enters just right of the barrier, moves through the remaining arrow, and becomes the product. The product and gauge turn green. Draw a bracket from the pathway start to the entry point labelled 'block lies before here'.
scenes.narration: Now add a downstream intermediate. It enters beyond the broken arrow. The later functions convert it into the needed product, and growth returns. Rescue places the block somewhere before that entry point.

scenes.tts: A new mutant blocks the last arrow. Which supply can restore growth: the early intermediate, or the final product? Trace each route before choosing.
scenes.caption: A new mutant blocks the last arrow. Which supply can restore growth: the early intermediate, or the final product? Trace each route before choosing.
scenes.visual: Reset every result to neutral. Move the red barrier to the last arrow. Place a blue early-intermediate supply beneath the left side and a green-outlined final-product supply beneath the right. Center 'Which restores growth?' above them. Do not reveal either route.
scenes.narration: A new mutant blocks the last arrow. Which supply can restore growth: the early intermediate, or the final product? Trace each route before choosing.

scenes.visual: Hold the question for thinking. The two candidate supplies drift slightly toward their entry points, then return. The final product, gauge, and answer remain neutral.

scenes.tts: The early intermediate still meets the last block, so it cannot rescue. The final product needs no remaining conversion. Supplying it restores growth. The useful supply entered after every blocked step.
scenes.caption: The early intermediate still meets the last block, so it cannot rescue. The final product needs no remaining conversion. Supplying it restores growth. The useful supply entered after every blocked step.
scenes.visual: Send the blue candidate along the path until it stops at the last red barrier; show no growth. Clear that answer. Then place the final-product block directly in the product slot; the gauge turns green. Highlight only the entry position after the barrier.
scenes.narration: The early intermediate still meets the last block, so it cannot rescue. The final product needs no remaining conversion. Supplying it restores growth. The useful supply entered after every blocked step.

scenes.tts: Compare several mutants. An early block is rescued by many later supplies. A middle block has fewer options. A late block may accept only the product. Nested rescue patterns let us read pathway order backward.
scenes.caption: Compare several mutants. An early block is rescued by many later supplies. A middle block has fewer options. A late block may accept only the product. Nested rescue patterns let us read pathway order backward.
scenes.visual: Duplicate the carried pathway into three large rows. Put the red barrier early, middle, then late. Supply blocks sweep across each row; green growth appears only for entry points to the right of that row's barrier. Align the nested green results into a staircase, labelled 'more rescue = earlier block' as a schematic inference.
scenes.narration: Compare several mutants. An early block is rescued by many later supplies. A middle block has fewer options. A late block may accept only the product. Nested rescue patterns let us read pathway order backward.

scenes.tts: This reading needs assumptions. The supplied compound must enter the cell and join the pathway. The pathway must behave like the tested chain. A rescue class can contain several genes, because different functions may act between the same supplies.
scenes.caption: This reading needs assumptions. The supplied compound must enter the cell and join the pathway. The pathway must behave like the tested chain. A rescue class can contain several genes, because different functions may act between the same supplies.
scenes.visual: Keep one pathway large. Animate a gate at the cell edge opening for a usable supply. Beside it, show a branching path only as a gray caution card marked 'different model'. Then place several small function badges between the same pair of supplied blocks, all under one bracket labelled 'one rescue class'.
scenes.narration: This reading needs assumptions. The supplied compound must enter the cell and join the pathway. The pathway must behave like the tested chain. A rescue class can contain several genes, because different functions may act between the same supplies.

scenes.tts: A strain can carry more than one block. An early supply may bypass the first barrier yet stop at a later one. Growth returns only when the supplied material enters after every remaining block.
scenes.caption: A strain can carry more than one block. An early supply may bypass the first barrier yet stop at a later one. Growth returns only when the supplied material enters after every remaining block.
scenes.visual: Place two red barriers on the carried pathway, one early and one late. A blue supply enters between them, passes the early position, then stops at the later barrier. Reset the gauge. A green-outlined product enters after both barriers and turns the growth gauge green.
scenes.narration: A strain can carry more than one block. An early supply may bypass the first barrier yet stop at a later one. Growth returns only when the supplied material enters after every remaining block.

scenes.tts: Complementation and feeding experiments ask related rescue questions, but their groups differ. Complementation groups sort mutations by shared function. Rescue classes sort blocks by pathway position. Keeping those readouts separate prepares us to compare function with recombination.
scenes.caption: Complementation and feeding experiments ask related rescue questions, but their groups differ. Complementation groups sort mutations by shared function. Rescue classes sort blocks by pathway position. Keeping those readouts separate prepares us to compare function with recombination.
scenes.visual: Split the frame. Left: the first film's chromosome pair gathers mutant dots into blue and gold complementation groups, labelled 'shared function'. Right: the pathway staircase gathers rows by entry position, labelled 'pathway position'. Bring both panels under a neutral heading 'rescue questions', without merging their groups.
scenes.narration: Complementation and feeding experiments ask related rescue questions, but their groups differ. Complementation groups sort mutations by shared function. Rescue classes sort blocks by pathway position. Keeping those readouts separate prepares us to compare function with recombination.

scenes.tts: Rescue narrows the possibilities; it does not expose the broken reaction directly. Measure accumulated compounds or test more intermediates when neighboring steps remain possible.
scenes.caption: Rescue narrows the possibilities; it does not expose the broken reaction directly. Measure accumulated compounds or test more intermediates when neighboring steps remain possible.
scenes.visual: Return to one pathway with a broad bracket labelled 'possible block region'. Add one new supply entry point; the bracket narrows but remains wider than one arrow. Beside it, animate a neutral sample tube under 'measure accumulation'. Keep all inferred locations schematic.
scenes.narration: Rescue narrows the possibilities; it does not expose the broken reaction directly. Measure accumulated compounds or test more intermediates when neighboring steps remain possible.

scenes.visual: End card, one line only: 'A usable supplement rescues only by entering after the blocked step.' Center the line in large type. No title, subtitle, logo, or smaller line.
